Before, every segment of any log whose MTIME > t_min counted. Evidence for fp-1: tools/bench/stage_d1_l2r2_prerun.log:1-133 is a FAIL prerun segment 07:54:30 (+27 s) older than its PASS records (prerun_records.jsonl, 08:00:25); the log's mtime came from the later PASS segment, so the launch was refused.

CLAIM: L4 fails because its FIXTURE, not the gate, is wrong. selftest_launch_gate.py:77 writes the pre-run records at time.time()-100 (2026-09-28), and :81-82 writes the "newer" failing run with a hard-coded START stamp `2026-09-24 20:00:00` and `BGRUN END rc=1 after 3s` - i.e. a run that by its own stamp ENDED four days BEFORE the records. The old gate only saw the file mtime (fresh), so it passed; the new gate reads the stamp. A real bgrun writes the real local time, so a genuinely newer failed run still has end > t_min and is still refused (tools/bench/selftest_c121_3_gatefp.py N1/N2/N3: 21/0). The fix would be to stamp the fixture with the current time, not to change the gate.

cases.known_answer: The claim is wrong: skipping the read when Q_work is full keeps the 20 OLDER queued frames and loses the newest (drop-new; lag up to 20 frames). The project's overload rule acq -> tracking is LATEST-WINS - discard the backlog, read the newest frame, gap recorded by the buffer number (docs/decisions.md:25; frame-ownership-design.md 'not drop-new'; d1-build-plan.md:1200 already refutes the same 'freshest wins' wording for an enqueue that skips on full). Lossy Enqueue Element is excluded (decisions.md:21), so latest-wins must be built otherwise (e.g. dequeue/flush the backlog), or acquisition and tracking stay sequential. User decision 2026-09-28 15:3x (commit f504b34).
